// Fixture for scripts/test-scripts.sh (wallclock-check): stored as .txt so the tree's
// Go tools never compile it. Every call below is allowed, each for its own reason.
package zzwallclockprobe

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ianglennon/coaming/proto/testsupport"
)

func TestWaitsOnlyAsAllowed(t *testing.T) {
	ch := make(chan struct{})
	// testsupport deadlines are generous.
	select {
	case <-ch:
	case <-time.After(testsupport.Deadline):
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), testsupport.Deadline)
	defer cancel()
	// A literal of 30 s or more is generous too.
	_, cancel2 := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second)
	defer cancel2()
	_ = time.NewTimer(2 * time.Minute)
	_ = time.NewTimer(time.Hour)
	// A measurement printed for people asserts nothing.
	start := time.Now()
	t.Logf("took %v", time.Since(start))
	// A reason at the end of the line, or on the line above.
	_ = time.After(10 * time.Millisecond) // wall-clock: paces a fake; no assertion depends on it
	// wall-clock: lower bound; a timer cannot fire early, so load can only lengthen it
	_ = time.Since(start)
	// A call named only in a comment is not a call: time.After(time.Millisecond)
	_ = &http.Client{Timeout: testsupport.Deadline}
	_ = &http.Client{Timeout: time.Minute}
	_ = &http.Client{Timeout: timeout}                  // a value held elsewhere is not on this line
	_ = &http.Server{ReadHeaderTimeout: time.Second}    // wall-clock: the fake answers headers at once; the window is not waited on
}
